description: An inert systemd unit and a listening port. On probation with the route it exercises.
why: Proves the systemd_units branch, the `unit` kind's registration and the scan marker -- and asserts that NOTHING is identified from a unit name. `systemd_prefixes` is registered in catalog/routes.yaml and carries no values: the obvious entry, `ai.openclaw.` mirroring the macOS launchd prefix, would have been a guess, because the launchd labels were read off a live install and no Linux unit name has been. test/test_matcher.py is what caught that. So `openclaw` is FORBIDDEN here even though the unit this scenario writes is named after it -- which is the strongest form of the assertion, and the one that would fail the day someone added the prefix without reading it off an install. The `unit` rows still ship as evidence: a kind absent from the registry would be dropped rather than unmatched, which is the `ext` bug.
known_gaps: Skips wherever there is no system dbus -- a container has none, which is what the kind=scan marker in queries/runtime-linux.sql exists to report. It runs for real on a GitHub ubuntu runner, where systemd is PID 1, and on every family under test/run-gce.sh and test/run-ec2.sh.

No agent's systemd unit name has been read off a real install, so this proves the query and the matcher and not any vendor's naming. The route is registered and carries no values for exactly that reason.
systemd user units (systemctl --user) are not visible to the table at all, and a per-user agent gateway is exactly the thing that would be one.
